# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-15 (Extended v120)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Autumn Year 4, evening—trap has sprung at 6 P.M.)**: Paris—Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Luxembourg gardens; le Petit-Picpus convent; M. Gillenormand's residences; English provincial towns (Dunstead, Staveford, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Gulhaven, Wilwick). **Environmental**: Spring—frost silvering hedges, smoke flat; Summer—warm air, sparrows, bees, gulls, salt/tar scent; Autumn/Winter transition—icy breeze, snow; **Current (Autumn Year 4, evening)**: Smoke from chimneys lies flat over fields, bell for vespers rings thinly across roofs, light went early, dog barked then went quiet.

## Primary Locations
**GORBEAU HOUSE**: 50-52 Salpêtrière district. **JONDRETTE DEN**: Abject, fetid, sordid. Furniture: straw chair, infirm table, crockery, two pallets, straw beds. Walls: leprous, seamed, obscene charcoal sketches, repulsive moisture. Fireplace with brazier filled burning charcoal (glowing hot, red with blue flame), pot, broken boards, suspended rags, bird-cage. Dormer window (four broken panes). Colored engraving "THE DREAM" (sleeping woman/child, eagle, Napoleon on blue column). Wooden panel with coarse daub painting (principal personage harsh foreign canvas style)—recently revealed. Two heaps: old iron/ropes and well-made rope-ladder with wooden rungs and two hooks. Verdigris candlestick with burning candle providing sole light. **Current state (evening, after 6 P.M.)**: Illuminated by candle; crisis occurring.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette
Valjean integrated as convent assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Cosette became convent scholar; believes Valjean is her father; adores him. Fauchelevent sole ally aware of full presence. **Present state (Autumn Year 4)**: Cosette about thirteen/fourteen years old; appeared in Jondrette hovel as charitable visitor with M. Leblanc.

## Javert's Pursuit
Attached to Paris police. **Status (Autumn Year 4)**: Tall man, square face, thin firm mouth, thick gray ferocious whiskers. **Action (present, evening)**: Received report from Marius regarding Jondrette ambush. Gave Marius two small steel pistols (each loaded two balls). Instructed Marius to hide, watch through wall hole, fire when crisis reached peak. Entered hovel, purchased chisel, positioned himself for ambush. Gave key to Marius.

## Marius Pontmercy: Development, Passion, and Crisis

**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years since left grandfather. **Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction regarding baron title and Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Lost medallion of black shagreen.

**Political evolution (Winter Year 3 → Spring Year 4)**: Converted to Bonapartism and republicanism; calmed through reverie. Sympathies to humanity over nation, woman over people, idea over deed.

**Material condition (Spring Year 4)**: Gorbeau cabinet 30 francs annually; sustenance 20 sous daily; clothing 100 francs; linen 100 francs. Total: 450 francs. Earned ~700 francs yearly. Refused advancement (1,500 francs) to preserve liberty.

**Grandfather quarrel**: Violent estrangement three years ago without rapprochement.

**Relationship with Friends of the A B C**: Met Courfeyrac; became good friends. Close to M. Mabeuf. Social activities: dined with Courfeyrac; breakfasted at Café Voltaire.

## The Mysterious Couple, Girl (Cosette), and Marius's Passion

**Initial six-month observation (over one year prior)**: Marius noticed man approximately sixty (M. Leblanc) and very young girl on Luxembourg bench daily. Man: retired military officer, robust, weary, kindly. Girl: thin, awkward, convent scholar dress.

**Six-month interruption**: Observation ceased.

**Reunion and girl's transformation (Summer Year 3)**: Girl became well-dressed young maiden; wore black damask dress, white crape bonnet, white gloves, carved Chinese ivory parasol handle, silken shoe.

**First meaningful glance and awakening (Spring Year 4)**: Their glances met. Marius resolved to dress differently. Following day wore new coat and observed her. Perceived she wore everyday clothes. His worship of his father retreated to depths.

**Love's arrival and transformation**: Brain felt on fire. She appeared wholly feminine and angelic. Vexed about dust on boots. Walked like madman; ate and spoke excitedly.

**Strategic approach (Spring Year 4)**: Combined stations behind trees with diplomacy. She bent upon Marius all reveries of virginal and passionate eye.

**M. Leblanc's response**: Noticed something. Often rose when Marius arrived and moved to adjacent bench. Stared intently at Marius.

**Escalation and handkerchief (Spring Year 4)**: Found handkerchief on bench—white, fine, perfumed, marked U. F. Marius thought "Ursule!" Kissed it, placed on heart during day, beneath lips at night.

**Leg incident and jealousy (Spring Year 4)**: May breeze lifted dress to height of garter. A leg of exquisite shape appeared. Marius was exasperated and furious. Girl hastily thrust down dress with divinely troubled motion. **Harsh and capricious jealousy of the flesh awakened in his heart.** When she passed, Marius darted sullen and ferocious glance. She gave slight backward movement: "Well, what is the matter?"

**Veteran encounter and paroxysm**: A bent, wrinkled veteran in Louis XV uniform bearing soldier's cross crossed walk. Marius perceived satisfied air; struck him aged cynic addressed him fraternal wink. **Marius reached paroxysm of jealousy.** "Perhaps he was there! Perhaps he saw!"

**M. Leblanc and girl's disappearance (Summer-Autumn Year 4)**: Summer passed, autumn came, winter arrived. Neither returned to Luxembourg. **Marius had but one thought—to gaze once more on that sweet and adorable face.** Fell into black melancholy. All was over.

**Self-reproach (Autumn Year 4)**: Heaped hundred reproaches on himself.

**Ball at Sceaux (September Year 4)**: Allowed himself taken to ball hoping to find her. Did not see her. Left friends, returned home on foot alone through night, weary, feverish.

**Miraculous rediscovery and action (Autumn Year 4, afternoon before crisis)**: **Marius perceived the girl (Cosette) in Jondrette hovel when she arrived with M. Leblanc.** "It was certainly she. Marius could hardly distinguish her through the luminous vapor which had suddenly spread before his eyes." **Marius shuddered in dismay, felt on brink of bursting into tears.** His heart palpitated; seemed to him he had lost his soul and just found it again. During entire visit, Marius lived in ecstasy; eyes remained fixed on girl; heart seized and wholly enveloped her. **He devoured her with his eyes. Could not believe divine creature was in midst of vile creatures in that monstrous lair. Seemed to him he beheld humming-bird in midst of toads.**

## The Jondrette Family and Ambush Plot—Crisis Point (Autumn Year 4, Evening)

**Scheme and principals**: Thénardier (alias Jondrette) arranged ambush. M. Leblanc arrived at 6 o'clock to bring sixty francs. Accomplices include Panchaud (alias Printanier, alias Bigrenaille) and other prowlers. **Status (evening, after 6 P.M., crisis occurring)**: Three men in blue linen blouses and black paper masks entered garret through door—first thin with iron-tipped cudgel, second colossus with butcher's pole-axe for slaughtering cattle, third with enormous stolen prison key. Three others armed themselves from old iron pile: one with heavy shears, one with weighing-tongs, one with hammer; positioned across entrance in silence. Old man opened eyes on bed; Jondrette woman seated beside him.

**M. Leblanc's response**: Very pale, scrutinizing everything around him like man understanding his predicament. Moved head with astonished and attentive slowness toward all surrounding heads. No fear in his air. Improvised intrenchment out of table; robust appearance emerged, placed formidable fist on chair back with astonishing gesture.

**Thénardier's monologue and escalation**: Thénardier spoke of wretchedness, wanting to have girls taught paper-box trade, requiring table with board, special stove, pot with three compartments, paring-knife, mould, hammer, pincers—all to earn four sous daily working fourteen hours, each box passing through hands thirteen times. Repeated with varying inflections: "There is nothing left for me but to throw myself into the river! I went down three steps at the side of the bridge of Austerlitz the other day for that purpose." As he spoke, Thénardier's eye was fixed on door; M. Leblanc's eye fixed on Thénardier. M. Leblanc seemed asking himself: "Is this man an idiot?"

**Thénardier's confrontation**: Thénardier advanced to table, leaned across candle, crossed arms, put angular ferocious jaw close to M. Leblanc's calm face, advancing as far as possible without forcing retreat. **In posture of wild beast about to bite, he exclaimed**, addressing M. Leblanc as "villain." Female Thénardier sprang from bed; Thénardier grasped chair as though to crush it, shouted to wife: "Don't you stir!"

**Thénardier's nature revealed**: In his words, accent, gesture, glance darting flames, in explosion of evil nature disclosing everything, mixture of braggadocio and abjectness, pride and pettiness, rage and folly, chaos of real griefs and false sentiments, immodesty of malicious man tasting voluptuous delights of violence, shameless nudity of repulsive soul, conflagration of all sufferings combined with all hatreds—**something as hideous as evil and as heart-rending as truth.**

**Marius's crisis of conscience**: Everything depended on Marius. Unknown to themselves, he held all those beings in his hand. If he fired pistol, M. Leblanc saved, Thénardier lost; if he did not fire, M. Leblanc sacrificed. Remorse awaited him either case. What should he choose? Be false to most imperious souvenirs, all solemn vows, most sacred duty, most venerated text? Ignore his father's testament or allow perpetration of crime? On one hand heard "his Ursule" supplicating for her father; on other, colonel commending Thénardier to his care. **He felt he was going mad. His knees gave way beneath him.** He had not time for deliberation—scene before his eyes hastening to catastrophe like whirlwind sweeping him away. **He was on verge of swooning.**

**Critical realization**: Marius regained some measure of control. Last possibility of doubt vanished. **Certainly was Thénardier of the will.** Marius shuddered at reproach of ingratitude directed against his father, which he was on point of so fatally justifying. **His perplexity was redoubled.**

## Friends of the A B C and Criminal Underground

**Friends of the A B C**: Secret society in embryonic state. Meetings back room Café Musain. Members: Enjolras, Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle/Laigle de Meaux, Joly, Grantaire. Declared themselves Friends of the A B C—_Abaissé_, the debased (the people).

**Philosophical discourse**: All human societies have subterranean dimensions. Beneath all mines lies deepest stratum—grave of shadows, cellar of blind, _Inferi_. Wild spectres roam here, almost beasts, almost phantoms. Two step-mothers: ignorance and misery. From suffering pass to crime. Man becomes dragon. All others above have one object—suppress it.

**Patron-Minette**: Criminal association members Babet, Gueulemer, Claquesous, Montparnasse. **Gueulemer**: Six feet high, Hercules. Lair: sewer of Arche-Marion. **Claquesous**: He was night. Addressed accomplices only in absolute darkness, back turned. Never seen without mask. Ventriloquist. **Function**: Four ruffians formed Proteus, furnish canvas for ambushes in Seine department.

## English Provincial Towns: Rumors and Mundane Activities

**Rumors/claims**: Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged (**confirmed by Lurald telling Ulrald Corrford**). Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (rumor, no body). **Dunstead granary fire set on purpose (confirmed: Luena Stenenridge confided to Rozek; Rozek confided to Pewyn Stenenridge)**. Kadan Corrley burned letter from Yera Haskick revealing mill ledger rewritten. Kassa Brackick confided mill ledger rewritten. Fenelle Lindmere confided Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family (**later told Peten Haskick**). Fenelle Lindmere read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints.

**Recent movements**: Peten Haskick packed single trunk and moved from Dunstead to Staveford. Lura followed him within the month.

**Mundane activities (Spring-Summer-Autumn Year 4)**: Volan Stenworth and others read almanac, mispronounced saints; bought ribbon and regretted it. Conversations about weather, harvest, lame horse, river up in spring. Lurald laughed at story nobody else found funny. Baker's boy late, line at oven long. Roads rutted and puddled after thaw. Lurald spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight. Marald Corrford fell asleep in chair before fire. Nelan Brackick gave Volia Brackick solemn promise to repair roof of chapel at Wilwick. **Current (Autumn Year 4)**: Marald argued with carter over price of sack of oats. Yera also argued with carter over price of sack of oats. Kassa Brackick and Pewyn Stenenridge asked "Will it rain?"; shrugs answered. Yewyn Corrford said "Price of salt is scandal"; Yedan agreed. Yedan walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Ismira Stenson counted coins twice, came up penny short. Matho Stenson hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step; read almanac aloud, mispronounced saints. Ismira and Matho talked of weather, harvest, lame horse. Ismira gave brass map to Matho. Matho spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight. "You look tired," Matho told Ismira, who did not deny it. Dalis Stenworth hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step. Pelde counted coins twice, came up penny short. Ulrald Corrford complained of aching back, as usual. Bremira Corrford complained of aching back, as usual.
